albertus.name: Albert the Great, St., O.P.
albertus.role: Scholastic Philosopher & Doctor of the Church
albertus.bio: Dominican friar, bishop, and teacher of Thomas Aquinas whose commentaries on Aristotle's Organon and Mathematics shaped medieval scholastic epistemology.

alexander.name: Alexander of Aphrodisias
alexander.bio: Foremost ancient Greek commentator on Aristotle, known in antiquity and the Middle Ages simply as 'The Commentator' before Averroes.
works: In Aristotelis Analyticorum Priorum Librum I Commentarium

alvarez-laso.name: José Alvarez Laso, C.M.F.
alvarez-laso.bio: Claretian scholar who authored a doctoral study under Hoenen on the philosophy of mathematics in St. Thomas Aquinas.
works: La Filosofía de las Matemáticas en Santo Tomás (1952)

occurrences.display: La Filosofia de las Matemáticas en Santo Tomás Mexico, 1952, pagg. 2-6

amaldi.name: Ugo Amaldi
amaldi.bio: Professor of mathematics in Rome and collaborator of Federigo Enriques on the foundations of elementary geometry and continuous transformation groups.
works: Sui concetti di retta e di piano (Questioni riguardanti le matematiche elementari)

occurrences.display: U. Amaldi « sui concetti di retta e di piano »

aquinas.name: St. Thomas Aquinas, O.P.
aquinas.bio: Dominican friar and Doctor of the Church whose synthesis of Aristotelian noetics—abstraction from phantasms, intelligible matter, and judgment by resolution to sensory principles—forms the central framework of Hoenen's treatise.
works: Expositio super Librum Boethii De Trinitate
In Aristotelis Libros Posteriorum Analyticorum Expositio
Commentaria in Octo Libros Physicorum Aristotelis

occurrences.display: I Sent. Dist. III q. 1 a. 2

aristotle.name: Aristotle
aristotle.bio: Founder of the Peripatetic school and formal logic, whose theory of demonstrative science (Analytica Posteriora), abstraction (τὰ ἐξ ἀφαιρέσεως), and intelligible matter (ὕλη νοητή) originates classical geometric epistemology.

baeumker.name: Clemens Baeumker
baeumker.bio: German Neo-Scholastic historian of philosophy whose authoritative study on the problem of matter in Greek philosophy is cited by Hoenen on Plato and Aristotle.
works: Das Problem der Materie in der griechischen Philosophie (1890)

occurrences.display: Cl. BAEUMKER, Das Problem der Materie in der Griechischen Philosophie pagg. 422 sqq.

becker.name: Oskar Becker
becker.bio: German philosopher and student of Husserl who wrote extensively on the phenomenological foundations of geometry and Eudoxian proportion theory.
works: Beiträge zur phänomenologischen Begründung der Geometrie (1923)

beltrami.name: Eugenio Beltrami
beltrami.bio: Pioneer of differential geometry who constructed the first concrete Euclidean models (pseudosphere) proving the relative consistency of non-Euclidean geometry.
works: Saggio di interpretazione della geometria non-euclidea (1868)

berkeley.name: George Berkeley
berkeley.bio: Bishop of Cloyne whose critique of abstract ideas and theory of sensory minima (minimum visibile) prepared Hume's radical empiricism.
works: A Treatise Concerning the Principles of Human Knowledge (1710)
An Essay Towards a New Theory of Vision (1709)

boethius.name: Anicius Manlius Severinus Boethius
boethius.bio: Late antique philosopher whose treatise De Trinitate occasioned Thomas Aquinas's celebrated commentary on the division and methods of the speculative sciences.

bonitz.name: Hermann Bonitz
bonitz.bio: German philologist and author of the indispensable Index Aristotelicus and commentary on Aristotle's Metaphysics.

brouwer.name: Luitzen Egbertus Jan Brouwer
brouwer.bio: Topologist and philosopher of mathematics who founded mathematical intuitionism, grounding mathematics in the primordial intuition of time rather than formalist axioms.

brunschvicg.name: Léon Brunschvicg
brunschvicg.role: French Idealist Philosopher & Historian of Mathematics
brunschvicg.bio: Co-founder of the Revue de Métaphysique et de Morale whose historical-critical study of mathematical philosophy is frequently examined by Hoenen.
works: Les étapes de la philosophie mathématique (1912)

occurrences.display: Les étapes de la philosophie mathématique pag. 338

burnet.name: John Burnet
burnet.bio: Professor of Greek at St Andrews whose editions of Plato and histories of early Greek philosophy shaped twentieth-century scholarship on Platonic hypotheses.

cajetan.name: Thomas de Vio Cajetan, Cardinal, O.P.
cajetan.bio: Master General of the Dominicans and classic commentator on the Summa Theologiae, who systematized the distinction between abstractio formalis and abstractio totalis.
works: In De Ente et Essentia Commentaria (1495)

cantor.name: Georg Cantor
cantor.role: German Mathematician & Creator of Set Theory
cantor.bio: Founder of transfinite set theory (Mengenlehre) and the arithmetic of the continuum, whose definitions of point-sets and continuity transformed modern analysis.

carteron.name: Henri Carteron
carteron.bio: Editor and translator of the Budé edition of Aristotle's Physics and author of a study on Aristotle's concept of force and motion.
works: La notion de force dans le système d'Aristote (1923)

christ.name: Wilhelm von Christ
christ.bio: Editor of the Teubner critical edition of Aristotle's Metaphysics.

couturat.name: Louis Couturat
couturat.bio: Champion of symbolic logic and Russellian logicism in France, editor of Leibniz's unpublished logical manuscripts, and critic of Kantian mathematical intuition.
works: La philosophie des mathématiques de Kant (1904)

descartes.name: René Descartes
descartes.bio: Founder of analytic geometry and modern rationalism; Hoenen critically examines both his coordinate reduction of extension and the intuitive nature of his Cogito ergo sum.

einstein.name: Albert Einstein
einstein.bio: Creator of special and general relativity; his 1921 lecture 'Geometrie und Erfahrung' famously distinguished purely axiomatic geometry from practical physical geometry.

enriques.name: Federigo Enriques
enriques.bio: Leader of the Italian school of algebraic geometry and editor of Questioni riguardanti le matematiche elementari, who analyzed the psychological and sensory origins of geometric concepts.

euclid.name: Euclid of Alexandria
euclid.bio: Author of the Elements, whose tripartite division of first principles into Definitions (ὅροι), Postulates (αἰτήματα), and Common Notions (κοιναὶ ἔννοιαι) embodies the Aristotelian demonstrative ideal.
works: Elementa (The Thirteen Books of the Elements)

eudoxus.name: Eudoxus of Cnidus
eudoxus.bio: Member of Plato's Academy who created the general theory of proportions (Elements Book V) and the method of exhaustion (Book XII) to resolve the crisis of incommensurables.
works: Theory of Proportions (preserved in Euclid, Elements V)

freudenthal.name: Hans Freudenthal
freudenthal.bio: Topologist and historian of mathematics who engaged directly with Hoenen in Gregorianum on the roles of intuition and abstraction in the foundations of geometry.
works: De fontibus geometriae in intuitione et abstractione quaerendis (Gregorianum, 1951)

gauss.name: Carl Friedrich Gauss
gauss.bio: Developed the intrinsic differential geometry of curved surfaces and privately discovered non-Euclidean geometry, questioning the a priori necessity of Euclidean space.

geyser.name: Joseph Geyser
geyser.bio: Professor of philosophy at Münster, Freiburg, and Munich, known for his studies on Aristotelian epistemology and critical realism.

occurrences.display: GEYSER, Die Erkenntnistheorie des Aristoteles, cap. VI et XII

gilson.name: Étienne Gilson
gilson.role: French Thomistic Philosopher & Historian of Medieval Philosophy
gilson.bio: Leading twentieth-century historian of medieval philosophy and proponent of existential Thomism, whose works on being, essence, and existential judgment Hoenen discusses in the Appendix.

gonseth.name: Ferdinand Gonseth
gonseth.bio: Professor at ETH Zürich who characterized mathematical objects as idealized 'schematic physics' (physique de l'objet quelconque) abstracted from experimental reality.

hadamard.name: Jacques Hadamard
hadamard.bio: Leading French analyst and geometer who investigated the psychology of mathematical invention and directed the mathematical volume of the Encyclopédie Française.
works: Encyclopédie Française, Tome I: L'Outillage Mental (1937)

occurrences.display: J. HADAMARD, Encycl. Franç I (1937) I-52-7

hamelin.name: Octave Hamelin
hamelin.bio: French idealist philosopher and historian of ancient philosophy whose posthumous lectures on the system of Aristotle are cited by Hoenen.

occurrences.display: O. HAMELIN, Le Système d'Aristote, pagg. 258 sq., 234 sq.

hardy.name: Godfrey Harold Hardy
hardy.bio: Leading Cambridge analyst and number theorist whose 1929 essay 'Mathematical Proof' defended genuine intellectual insight against purely formalist symbol-games.

hasse.name: Helmut Hasse
hasse.bio: Algebraist and number theorist who co-authored with Heinrich Scholz a celebrated treatise on the foundational crisis of Greek mathematics triggered by incommensurability.
works: Die Grundlagenkrisis der griechischen Mathematik (with H. Scholz, 1928)

occurrences.display: H. HASSE und H. SCHOLZ, Die Grundlagenkrisis der Griechischen Mathematik in Kantstudien (1928) pagg. 4-34

hausdorff.name: Felix Hausdorff
hausdorff.role: German Mathematician & Founder of General Topology
hausdorff.bio: Creator of the theory of topological and metric spaces (Hausdorff spaces) and author of philosophical essays on the problem of physical and geometric space.

occurrences.display: F. HAUSDORF, Das Raumproblem in Annalen der Naturphilosophie III (1904) pag. 3

heath.name: Sir Thomas Little Heath
heath.role: British Historian of Ancient Greek Mathematics
heath.bio: Foremost English translator and commentator of Euclid, Archimedes, and Apollonius, whose monumental commentary on Euclid's Elements is a primary source for Hoenen.
works: The Thirteen Books of Euclid's Elements (1908; 2nd ed. 1926)

occurrences.display: Th. Heath in suo opere famoso A History of Greek Mathematics, Oxford 1921, I pagg. 335 sqq.

hegel.name: Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel
hegel.bio: Architect of absolute idealism whose remarks on Euclid's definitions and postulates in the Wissenschaft der Logik are examined by Hoenen.

occurrences.display: HEGEL , Wissenschaft der Logik II I k. 3 Anmerkung. Werke (ed. 1834) pagg. 142 sq.

helmholtz.name: Hermann von Helmholtz
helmholtz.role: German Physicist, Physiologist & Philosopher of Science
helmholtz.bio: Investigated the physiological optics of spatial perception and characterized physical geometry through the free mobility of rigid bodies (Riemann-Helmholtz space problem).
works: Über die Tatsachen, die der Geometrie zum Grunde liegen (1868)
Über den Ursprung und die Bedeutung der geometrischen Axiome (1870)

hessenberg.name: Gerhard Hessenberg
hessenberg.bio: Geometer and foundational theorist known for his work on projective geometry (Desargues's and Pascal's theorems) and philosophical critique of mathematical axiomatics.
works: Kritik und System in Mathematik und Philosophie (1908)

hilbert.name: David Hilbert
hilbert.bio: Author of Grundlagen der Geometrie (1899), which replaced intuitive definitions with implicit axiomatic characterization of incidence, order, congruence, parallels, and continuity.

hoelder.name: Otto Hölder
hoelder.bio: Group theorist and analyst who authored a major philosophical treatise on the mathematical method, axiomatic deduction, and genetic construction.
works: Anschauung und Denken in der Geometrie (1900)

hoenen.name: Petrus Hubertus Jacobus Hoenen, S.J.
hoenen.bio: Professor of Cosmology and Philosophy of Mathematics at the Pontifical Gregorian University in Rome; author of De Noetica Geometriae and La théorie du jugement d'après St. Thomas d'Aquin.
works: De Noetica Geometriae: Origine Theoriae Cognitionis (1954)
La théorie du jugement d'après St. Thomas d'Aquin (1946; 2nd ed. 1953)
Reality and Judgment According to St. Thomas (1952)

hume.name: David Hume
hume.bio: Radical empiricist who attacked the exactness of Euclidean geometry in the Treatise by reducing space to discrete sensory minima (minimum visibile) incapable of infinite divisibility.

kant.name: Immanuel Kant
kant.bio: Characterized geometric propositions as synthetic a priori judgments grounded in pure intuition of space as an a priori form of sensibility—a doctrine Hoenen contrasts with Aristotelian abstraction from sensible phantasms.
works: Prolegomena zu einer jeden künftigen Metaphysik (1783)

killing.name: Wilhelm Killing
killing.bio: Co-discoverer of Lie algebras (Killing form) and professor at Münster who wrote a comprehensive two-volume treatise on the foundations of Euclidean and non-Euclidean geometry.
works: Einführung in die Grundlagen der Geometrie (1893–1898)

klein.name: Felix Klein
klein.bio: Author of the Erlangen Program classifying geometries by transformation groups, and originator of the philosophical distinction between Approximationsmathematik (empirical perception bounded by a threshold) and Präzisionsmathematik (idealized limits).
works: Vergleichende Betrachtungen über neuere geometrische Forschungen (Erlanger Programm, 1872)
Anwendung der Differential- und Integralrechnung auf Geometrie: Eine Revision der Prinzipien (1902; 2nd ed. 1907)
Elementarmathematik vom höheren Standpunkte aus (3rd ed. 1925)

leibniz.name: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz
leibniz.bio: Co-inventor of the infinitesimal calculus and pioneer of symbolic logic (characteristica universalis) and analysis situs, who sought to reduce all mathematical truths to identities demonstrable via definitions.

locke.name: John Locke
locke.bio: Author of An Essay Concerning Human Understanding, whose conceptualist account of abstract general ideas was critiqued by Berkeley, Hume, and Leibniz.

lonergan.name: Bernard Lonergan, S.J.
lonergan.bio: Studied under Hoenen at the Gregorian University; his Verbum articles (1946–1949) and Insight (1957) developed Hoenen's discovery of Aquinas's doctrine of intellectual insight into phantasms.
works: The Concept of Verbum in the Writings of St. Thomas Aquinas (1946–1949)
Insight: A Study of Human Understanding (1957)

occurrences.display: P. B. Lonergan, The concept of « verbum » in the writings of St. Thomas Aquinas in Theological Studies 1946 pagg. 349-392, 1947 pagg. 35-79, 404-44 ; pro hoc puncto I pag. 353

maier.name: Anneliese Maier
maier.role: German Historian of Late Medieval Science & Philosophy
maier.bio: Archival scholar at the Vatican Library whose groundbreaking studies illuminated fourteenth-century Scholastic natural philosophy and mathematics.
works: An der Grenze von Scholastik und Naturwissenschaft (1943)

occurrences.display: Anneliese Maier, An der Grenze von Scholastik und Naturwissenschaft, 1943 pagg. 312 sqq.

mercier.name: Désiré-Joseph Cardinal Mercier
mercier.role: Belgian Neo-Scholastic Philosopher & Founder of the Louvain Institute
mercier.bio: Founder of the Higher Institute of Philosophy at Louvain; Hoenen critiques Mercier's purely conceptualist ('analytic') interpretation of necessary judgments.

meyerson.name: Émile Meyerson
meyerson.role: Polish-born French Philosopher of Science & Epistemologist
meyerson.bio: Analyzed the actual progression of scientific and mathematical thought (le cheminement de la pensée) as a tension between rational identification and the resistance of the real.

mill.name: John Stuart Mill
mill.bio: Argued in A System of Logic that geometric definitions describe non-existent idealizations and that axioms are merely inductive generalizations from sensory experience.
works: A System of Logic, Ratiocinative and Inductive (1843; 5th ed. 1862)

moebius.name: August Ferdinand Möbius
moebius.bio: Pioneer of projective geometry and topology; discovered the non-orientable one-sided surface (folium Moebii / Möbius strip), which Hoenen analyzes in detail in Caput III.
works: Über die Bestimmung des Inhaltes eines Polyëders (1865)

newton.name: Sir Isaac Newton
newton.bio: Author of the Principia Mathematica and co-founder of the calculus (method of fluxions); defended absolute space and time and the kinematic generation of geometric magnitudes.

parmenides.name: Parmenides of Elea
parmenides.bio: Founder of the Eleatic school who affirmed the unity and immutability of Being and denied the reality of motion and division.

pasch.name: Moritz Pasch
pasch.bio: Pioneered the rigorous axiomatization of projective and order geometry (Pasch's Axiom), insisting that geometric deduction must proceed independently of intuitive diagrams once nuclear axioms (Kern-Sätze) are abstracted from experience.

peano.name: Giuseppe Peano
peano.bio: Formulated the Peano axioms for arithmetic, symbolic mathematical logic, and the space-filling Peano curve (1890) challenging naive intuitions of dimension.
works: I principii di geometria logicamente esposti (1889)
Sur une courbe, qui remplit toute une aire plane (1890)

philoponus.name: John Philoponus
philoponus.bio: Late antique commentator on Aristotle's Physics and Posterior Analytics who developed the theory of three-dimensional spatial extension (διάστημα) and impetus.

plato.name: Plato
plato.bio: Founder of the Athenian Academy; his Divided Line (Republic VI) assigned mathematical objects to discursive understanding (διάνοια) proceeding from hypotheses with the aid of visible diagrams.

poincare.name: Henri Poincaré
poincare.role: French Mathematician, Physicist & Philosopher of Science
poincare.bio: Universal mathematician and creator of algebraic topology (analysis situs) who argued that geometric axioms are neither synthetic a priori judgments nor experimental facts, but conventions (disguised definitions) guided by experience.

proclus.name: Proclus Lycius Diadochus
proclus.bio: Head of the Athenian Neoplatonic Academy whose Commentary on Book I of Euclid's Elements is the primary ancient source on the history and philosophy of Greek geometry and imagination (φαντασία) as passive intellect.
works: In Primum Euclidis Elementorum Librum Commentarii

protagoras.name: Protagoras of Abdera
protagoras.bio: Sophist who argued against geometers that sensible circles and rulers touch at more than a single indivisible point (reported by Aristotle, Metaphysics III 2, 997b35).

pythagoras.name: Pythagoras of Samos
pythagoras.bio: Founder of the Pythagorean brotherhood, which discovered the mathematical ratios of musical harmony, the Pythagorean theorem, and the incommensurability of the diagonal with the side.

reichenbach.name: Hans Reichenbach
reichenbach.role: German Philosopher of Science & Logical Empiricist
reichenbach.bio: Founder of the Berlin Circle who analyzed relativistic spacetime geometry via 'coordinative definitions' (Zuordnungsdefinitionen) and critiqued geometric visualization.

occurrences.display: H. REICHENBACH, Philos. der Raum-Zeit-Lehre (1928) pag. 10

riehl.name: Alois Riehl
riehl.bio: Representative of critical realism within Neo-Kantianism whose essays on logic and epistemology are cited by Hoenen.

occurrences.display: A. RIEHL. Logik und Erkenntnistheorie in Kultur der Gegenwart Abt. VI ed. 3 (1921) pag. 71

ross.name: Sir William David Ross
ross.bio: Provost of Oriel College, Oxford, and general editor of the Oxford Translation of Aristotle; his critical editions and commentaries on Aristotle's Metaphysics, Physics, and Analytics are frequently cited by Hoenen.

russell.name: Bertrand Russell
russell.bio: Co-author of Principia Mathematica and leading proponent of logicism, who defined pure mathematics as the class of all formal implications 'p implies q' containing only logical constants and variables.
works: An Essay on the Foundations of Geometry (1897)

scholz.name: Heinrich Scholz
scholz.role: German Logician, Philosopher & Historian of Mathematics
scholz.bio: Founder of the Münster school of mathematical logic; co-authored with Helmut Hasse the study on the foundational crisis of Greek mathematics.
works: Die Grundlagenkrisis der griechischen Mathematik (with H. Hasse, 1928)
Warum haben die Griechen die Irrationalzahlen nicht aufgebaut? (1928)

occurrences.display: H. HASSE und H. SCHOLZ, Die Grundlagenkrisis der Griechischen Mathematik in Kantstudien (1928) pagg. 4-34

simplicius.name: Simplicius of Cilicia
simplicius.bio: Student of Ammonius and Damascius whose encyclopedic commentaries on Aristotle's Physics and De Caelo preserve crucial fragments of Eudemus, Hippocrates of Chios, and ancient geometry.

stammler.name: Gerhard Stammler
stammler.bio: Neo-Kantian philosopher at Halle who analyzed the history of the number concept since Gauss and the logical theory of concepts, judgments, and inferences.

occurrences.display: G. STAMMLER in Begriff, Urteil, Schlusz, Halle-Saale 1928, pagg. 229, 245

study.name: Eduard Study
study.bio: Differential and algebraic geometer at Bonn who defended scientific realism in geometry against positivism and conventionalism.
works: Die realistische Weltansicht und die Lehre vom Raume (1914)

taylor.name: Alfred Edward Taylor
taylor.bio: Professor of Moral Philosophy at St Andrews and Edinburgh, renowned for his commentary on Plato's Timaeus and comprehensive study of Plato's dialogues.
works: Plato: The Man and His Work (1926)

theaetetus.name: Theaetetus of Athens
theaetetus.bio: Associate of Plato's Academy who classified quadratic irrationals (Euclid, Elements Book X) and completed the construction of the five regular polyhedra (Book XIII).
works: Theory of Irrationals & Regular Solids (in Euclid, Elements X & XIII)

themistius.name: Themistius
themistius.bio: Composed lucid paraphrases of Aristotle's Posterior Analytics, Physics, and De Anima that were widely studied by Arabic and Latin Scholastics.

trendelenburg.name: Friedrich Adolf Trendelenburg
trendelenburg.bio: Leader of the nineteenth-century Aristotelian revival in Germany, editor of De Anima, and critic of Hegelian dialectic and Kantian subjectivity.

vallee-poussin.name: Charles-Jean de la Vallée Poussin
vallee-poussin.bio: Professor at Louvain who proved the Prime Number Theorem independently of Hadamard and authored the classic Cours d'Analyse Infinitésimale.

voss.name: Aurel Voss
voss.bio: Differential geometer at Munich who authored influential philosophical surveys on the nature of mathematical knowledge.

waitz.name: Theodor Waitz
waitz.bio: Edited the standard nineteenth-century critical Greek edition and Latin commentary of Aristotle's Organon.

occurrences.display: TH. WAITZ in suo Commentario in Anal. Priora I 23 ; in eius editione I pagg. 427-429

weber.name: Heinrich Martin Weber
weber.bio: Algebraist and co-editor with Josef Wellstein of the Enzyklopädie der Elementarmathematik.

occurrences.display: Weber-Wellstein Enzyklopaedie der Elementar-Mathematik II (3 ed. 1925)
Weber-Wellstein in Enzyklopaedie der Elementarmathematik II Elemente der Geometrie (ed. 3 1915) pagg. 33-62

wellstein.name: Josef Wellstein
wellstein.bio: Professor at Strasbourg and co-author with Heinrich Weber of the Enzyklopädie der Elementarmathematik, whose chapters on the foundations of geometry are extensively analyzed by Hoenen.
works: Grundlagen der Geometrie (in Weber-Wellstein, Enzyklopädie der Elementarmathematik II, 1915 / 1925)

weyl.name: Hermann Weyl
weyl.bio: Student of Hilbert who contributed fundamentally to group representations, differential geometry, gauge theory, and the philosophy of the mathematical continuum.

occurrences.display: H. WEYL, Philosophie der Mathematik und Naturwissenschaft (1927) pag. 18

whitehead.name: Alfred North Whitehead
whitehead.bio: Co-author with Bertrand Russell of Principia Mathematica and creator of the method of extensive abstraction for deriving geometric points and instants from overlapping physical events.
works: An Enquiry Concerning the Principles of Natural Knowledge (1919)
